Intra-axial lesion with thick, irregular ring enhancement, central necrosis and FLAIR hyperintensity extending beyond the enhancing part: in an adult over 50 years this is the typical picture of glioblastoma. According to the WHO 2021 classification, glioblastoma is by definition IDH wild-type, grade 4.
Main differential diagnosis: metastasis (often rounder, at the corticosubcortical junction, with disproportionate edema and sometimes multiple), lymphoma (homogeneous enhancement, diffusion restriction, periventricular or corpus callosum location), abscess (thin, smooth wall, contents with diffusion restriction).
In the report: location and lobes involved, relationship with eloquent areas and ventricles, size of the enhancing part (for RANO assessment at follow-up), FLAIR extent, mass effect.
